summary: Headless lifecycle: (1) SIGTERM installs a one-shot sigaction handler (SA_RESTART|SA_RESETHAND) that only sets an AtomicBool; the async host loop observes it as an implicit shutdown (stop reading, emergency-cancel approvals, SHUTDOWN_GRACE, runtime shutdown), so in-flight work gets its terminal response, a shutdown ack {closing,drained} is written, the WAL is closed and the process exits 0. (2) EOF drain is bounded: HeadlessOptions.eof_drain (default 600s; ZENPI_HEADLESS_EOF_DRAIN_SECS or --eof-drain-secs N) after which the runtime is shut down and admitted work is cancelled with a terminal response. (3) Close hooks of owners still held by a detached job run on the cleanup thread, which the host now waits on (bounded, 10s) before returning. (4) A non-blocking flock EWOULDBLOCK maps to SessionError::Locked (code session_locked); the WAL open retry keys on it, and both the host and the CLI startup path emit a v2 JSONL error frame with code session_locked on stdout and exit non-zero with 'session_locked' on stderr. New public API: HeadlessOptions, run_stdio_owned_with, run_async_streams_with, install_termination_handler, write_startup_error, SessionError::code.
commands_run: sh /tmp/ze24x/oneshot.sh target/debug/zenpi  # printf '{"version":2,"id":"p1","type":"prompt","message":"hi"}\n' | zenpi --mode headless --auto --backend echo --session <tmp>; echo exit=$?
sh /tmp/ze24x/locked.sh target/debug/zenpi  # holder on a fifo, second zenpi on the same --session

Before the change the second process printed 'session I/O: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)'

notes: unsafe: sigaction install in src/headless.rs (install_termination_handler) and libc::kill in tests/headless_lifecycle.rs both carry // SAFETY: comments; the pre-existing flock call in src/session.rs lock_exclusive gained one. No new non-test unwrap/expect/panic, no new Arc<Mutex>. core.rs changes are CLI wiring only: --eof-drain-secs flag, handler install, a run()/run_host() split so a startup session_locked error is reported as a JSONL frame for headless clients. The one-shot validator already passed before this change; it is now covered by a test. SIGTERM after an explicit shutdown is already pending is a no-op; the handler is SA_RESETHAND so a second SIGTERM kills immediately. EOF drain default is 600s so long one-shot turns are not cut short. A binary started under parallel test load can take several seconds to reach its provider call, so the lifecycle tests use 60s bounds.
